previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted with chest pain and severe nausea and vomiting. Initial concerns for cardiac or pulmonary causes were ruled out with a normal EKG and chest X-ray. She developed coffee-ground emesis, suggesting upper gastrointestinal bleeding likely due to gastritis or a Mallory-Weiss tear, but declined endoscopy. Her symptoms were managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, acid suppression, and pain control. Anxiety and chronic back pain were also addressed during the admission. Her condition improved with supportive care, and she was transitioned from NPO to a regular diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume her usual medications and follow up with GI, endocrinology, and psychiatry.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, with hemorrhage

# Rectal bleeding/Lower GI bleed:  This was scant per patient 
report.  She was guaiac-negative on admission and had no further 
episodes.  Her HCT was stable.  ESR was normal, making 
inflammatory bowel disease unlikely.
.
# Diarrhea:  This self-resolved.  Her Reglan dose was halved.
.
# Nausea/vomiting:  This is a chronic issue and may be due to 
her gastroparesis.  She required IV Zofran.  She was tolerating 
meals by discharge.  She was discharged with Zofran ODT.
.
# DM1, uncontrolled:  Although her blood sugars were labile, she 
was never in DKA.  She was continued on her home insulin 
regimen.
.
# Anxiety/panic attacks:  Patient has frequent panic attacks.  
She was continued on sertraline and trazadone.  She required a 
few doses of lorazepam.
.
# Chronic low back pain:  She required IV hydromorphone initally 
while she had nausea/vomiting and was transitioned to po 
hydromorphone.  She will continue her home regimen of pain 
medications upon discharge.
.
# Hyperlipidemia:  She was continued on Ezetimibe.
